monsterGroup.name: Chromatic Dragons
entries: Chromatic dragons are the most numerous, powerful, and evil of true dragons. They are aggressive, hoarding, and gleefully cruel, the color of their scales betraying their preferred breath weapon and disposition: {@creature Black Dragon|MM|black} (acid, swamps and marshes), {@creature Blue Dragon|MM|blue} (lightning, deserts), {@creature Green Dragon|MM|green} (poison, forests), {@creature Red Dragon|MM|red} (fire, mountains), and {@creature White Dragon|MM|white} (cold, arctic ranges).

Every chromatic dragon serves as a stronghold-holding tyrant of its region, exacting tribute from the sentient creatures nearby and collecting a hoard of treasure. All chromatic dragons age through five recognized stages—wyrmling, young, adult, ancient, and (rarely) greatwyrm—growing in size, cunning, and magical potency at each step. They are ultimately the children of Tiamat, the five-headed Queen of Evil Dragons.

signatureAbilities.name: Frightful Presence
entries: Every adult and ancient chromatic dragon radiates a supernatural aura of terror. Creatures of the dragon's choice within a wide radius that can see it must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or be {@condition frightened} for 1 minute; a target that succeeds is immune to the same dragon's Frightful Presence for 24 hours.

signatureAbilities.name: Breath Weapon
entries: Each chromatic dragon exhales a devastating cone or line of elemental energy keyed to its color—acid, lightning, poison gas, fire, or cold. The shape, save DC, and damage die scale sharply from wyrmling to ancient.

monsterGroup.name: Metallic Dragons
entries: Metallic dragons are noble, honorable, and (with rare exception) good-aligned true dragons whose scales gleam like the metals they take their names from: {@creature Brass Dragon|MM|brass} (fire, deserts), {@creature Bronze Dragon|MM|bronze} (lightning, coastal), {@creature Copper Dragon|MM|copper} (acid, hills and stony rises), {@creature Gold Dragon|MM|gold} (fire, temperate anywhere), and {@creature Silver Dragon|MM|silver} (cold, mountaintops and clouds).

Metallic dragons are the offspring of Bahamut, the Platinum Dragon and lord of good dragonkind, and are the ancestral foes of the chromatic dragons. All metallics can adopt humanoid or beast forms, allowing them to walk among mortals unseen—many spend their long adult lives as scholars, sages, or wandering guardians before finally retiring to lair as ancients.

signatureAbilities.name: Change Shape
entries: All adult and ancient metallic dragons can magically polymorph into a humanoid or beast of a challenge rating no greater than their own (though certain statistics remain). This is the primary way metallics interact with mortal society.

signatureAbilities.name: Two Breath Weapons
entries: Uniquely among true dragons, each metallic dragon possesses two breath weapons: one damaging elemental breath, and one non-damaging "utility" breath (sleep gas, repulsion gas, slow gas, weakening gas, paralyzing breath, or similar) that reflects the dragon's temperament.

monsterGroup.name: Slaadi
entries: The slaadi are enormous, frog-like humanoids native to Limbo, the plane of pure chaos. They embody unfettered disorder—vicious, capricious, and driven by an ever-shifting compulsion to reproduce, hunt, and multiply. Their society, such as it is, is loosely ruled by the {@creature Slaad, Death|MM|Death Slaadi} and the twin slaad lords Ssendam and Ygorl, but any given slaad is more likely to devour its siblings than serve them.

Slaadi are categorized by the color of their hides, which corresponds to a rigid ecological hierarchy: {@creature Slaad, Red|MM|Red} and {@creature Slaad, Blue|MM|Blue} are the numerous "infectors," spreading the slaad race through implanted eggs and Chaos Phage; {@creature Slaad, Green|MM|Green} are shape-shifting spies and wanderers; {@creature Slaad, Gray|MM|Gray} and {@creature Slaad, Death|MM|Death} are the powerful, spellcasting elders.

signatureAbilities.name: Chaos Phage
entries: A red slaad's claw can implant an egg, while a blue slaad's claw transmits a disease that transforms the victim over days into a new slaad. The Chaos Phage life cycle is how slaadi propagate across the Material Plane.

signatureAbilities.name: Shapechanging (Green and Death)
entries: Green and death slaadi can assume the form of a Small or Medium humanoid at will, allowing them to infiltrate mortal societies and sow chaos from within.

monsterGroup.name: Modrons
entries: Modrons are the geometric, hive-minded constructs of Mechanus, the plane of perfect law and mechanism. Each modron occupies a fixed rung in a rigid hierarchy—{@creature Monodrone|MM|monodrones} (single sphere) do the plane's most menial tasks, {@creature Duodrone|MM|duodrones} carry them out, {@creature Tridrone|MM|tridrones} enforce order among them, {@creature Quadrone|MM|quadrones} command patrols, and {@creature Pentadrone|MM|pentadrones} rule regions.

Above the base modrons stand the hierarchs: decatons, nonatons, octons, septons, hextons, quintons, quartons, tertians, secundi, and finally the near-divine Primus. When a superior modron is destroyed, an inferior is elevated in its place, its form spontaneously reconfiguring—a process the modrons themselves regard with clockwork indifference. Every seventeen years, a Great Modron March sweeps across the outer planes.

signatureAbilities.name: Axiomatic Mind
entries: Modrons cannot be compelled to act in a manner contrary to their duty or Modron nature; they are immune to spells and effects that would alter their alignment or force disobedience.

signatureAbilities.name: Disintegration
entries: When a modron dies, its body disintegrates into a fine dust, leaving no trace—a courtesy the hierarchy extends to all of its own, and to no one else.

monsterGroup.name: Yugoloths
entries: Yugoloths are the mercenary fiends of Gehenna, the plane of avarice. They pledge no allegiance to Abyss or Nine Hells; they serve whichever archdevil, demon prince, or mortal invoker can afford them, and betray that patron the moment a better offer arrives.

The yugoloth order is stratified by function: {@creature Mezzoloth|MM|mezzoloths} are the shock troops, {@creature Nycaloth|MM|nycaloths} the aerial cavalry, {@creature Arcanaloth|MM|arcanaloths} the sorcerous secretaries who broker contracts, and {@creature Ultroloth|MM|ultroloths} the terrifying generals. Above them all sits the mysterious General of Gehenna. The MPMM lineup adds the amphibious {@creature Hydroloth|MPMM|hydroloth}, the mind-melting {@creature Oinoloth|MPMM|oinoloth}, and others.

signatureAbilities.name: Contracted Service
entries: Every summoned yugoloth serves under a specific, negotiated contract. Break the contract and the yugoloth is under no obligation to obey—typically it turns on the summoner immediately.

signatureAbilities.name: Innate Teleportation
entries: All yugoloths can teleport at will, allowing them to disengage from any fight that turns against them and reappear where the contract is more profitable.
